_comment: Shared recognition contract of the two mail gates (scripts/hooks/outgoing-copy-gate.py :: is_send_invocation and scripts/email-send-gate.mjs :: isSendInvocation). The conformance test (send-invocation-conformance.test.ts) runs EVERY case through BOTH implementations and asserts both equal `expected` -- divergence between the two copies surfaces as a test failure, not an incident (SUBGATEPOZ822, msg 14289). Unparseable-input fallbacks are deliberately NOT here: the two gates fall back differently by design (copy-gate: strong literals; hard-gate: full legacy patterns) and each pins its own in its scope test. A [marveen:...] prefixu esetek Marveen fuggetlen review-probai (store/marveen-send-gate-cases.json, msg 14302) -- a 'hatar' jeloles tortenete: az ot naiv exec-alak 2026-08-22 delutan LEZARULT (expected true), a megmaradt dokumentalt korlat az elfedett/futasidoben osszerakott kod; egy kesobbi valtozasnak itt teszt-hibakent kell jelentkeznie MINDKET iranyban, a nema atbillenes a tiltott allapot. INTERAGENTHOMOGLIF923 (2026-09-23): the inter-agent `curl .../api/messages` cases STAY expected:false here -- they are NOT email sends, and NONE of the email copy rules (accents, name rule, em dash) run on them. What changed is OUTSIDE this contract: the copy gate runs a SEPARATE, homoglyph-only check on that path (outgoing-copy-gate.py :: inter_agent_homoglyph_gate), blocking on a mixed-script word and passing an uninterpretable body with a loud warning. A reader must not take the expected:false rows as 'the path is unguarded', nor that change as 'the full copy gate now runs there'. graph-forward (Brainy 2958, N1): the Graph CLI (graph-mail.ts) is classified by an ALLOWLIST of its subcommand -- verify, list and show are reads, every other word after the CLI file name (forward, send, FORWARD, `--`, a flag, a variable, none) is a send, where the file runs as a program or behind a node-like or package runner; forwardMail joins sendMail in the code-string rules. On an unparseable command BOTH twins now fall back to the same graph-mail literal (any mention counts), so the T3 cases (`echo $'it\'s'; ... graph-mail.ts send`) are in this shared list despite the fallback note above. QUOTEPARITY1018: both tokenizers read ANSI-C `$'...'`, `$"..."`, line continuations and `#` comments the way the shell does, and the send classifier reads every command twice, with and without comments (a send in either reading counts); the QUOTEPARITY1018 rows were checked against real bash and zsh with stubbed senders (the two rows marked as stricter than the shell are deliberate).
